interface.name: easi_files_v1

description.summary: files between the person and the browser

interface.description: Offered only to the browser container's own launcher, on the browser's Wayland socket, and bound at most once per display: files move as descriptors, so the display never opens a path the browser can write. A download streams in on one end of a Unix stream socket pair the launcher writes as the browser writes the file (the display only ever reads it without blocking); uploads come in as pipes the launcher drains into its own private directory, and leave it once nothing can reach them. Every request and event belongs to the current control lease: the display drops what a lease change makes stale.

request.name: start_download

description.summary: the browser started a download

request.description: A download the launcher numbered `id`: its bytes arrive in order on `data` (one end of a Unix stream socket pair) as the browser writes them, and the stream ends with end_download or fail_download. The display offers it to the person holding control, and answers reading once someone receives it or stop_download when it will read no more. `known` says whether the browser knows its size (then exactly `size_hi`:`size_lo` bytes, or it fails); the display offers it with that size.

request.name: end_download

description.summary: every byte of a download was written to its socket

request.description: The browser finished the download; it is exactly this size, and the socket was closed after its last byte.

request.name: fail_download

description.summary: a download cannot be completed

request.description: The browser cancelled it, or wrote it in a way the launcher could not follow (it restarted the file): the person's download must fail rather than complete.

request.name: open_chooser

description.summary: the page opened a file chooser

request.description: The page asked for files (through the file chooser portal); the display asks the person holding control. Answered by chosen events and then chooser_done, or by chooser_cancelled.

request.name: close_chooser

description.summary: the page gave up on the chooser

request.description: Chromium closed its request: the display stops asking the person, and nothing more is sent for this chooser.

request.name: stored

description.summary: an upload is on disk

request.description: The launcher wrote all of an upload's bytes, exactly its size, to path (in its private uploads directory).

description.summary: an upload could not be stored

request.name: page_opened

description.summary: the answer to open_page

request.description: Whether the browser opened request `request`'s page (1) or not (0): the launcher answers every open_page once.

request.name: tab_refused

description.summary: a new tab was closed as it opened

request.description: The browser already kept the `limit` tabs a session may keep, so the launcher closed a new one as it opened: the display tells whoever acts in the session (the agent, at its next tool result).

request.name: tab_crashed

description.summary: a tab's page crashed

request.description: The process of a page the browser keeps in a tab ended: the kernel ended it as the browser reached its memory limit (memory 1), or it crashed some other way (0). The tab stays, showing the browser's error page: the display tells whoever acts in the session (the agent, at its next tool result).

request.name: browser_started

description.summary: the browser's process

request.description: The browser runs as process `pid`, in the launcher's PID namespace, which the agent's driver shares: said at each launch, a relaunch included. The display answers the admin with it (its `w` line), for a window the driver lists without one.

request.name: settled

description.summary: the browser has handled the keys before a settle

request.description: Answers settle: every page and frame of the browser has run what it had to run before, the key events sent to it among it, twice over, so the browser has had their answers too (a shortcut a page did not take moves the keyboard's focus only when the page's answer comes back).

event.name: reading

description.summary: someone is receiving the download

event.description: The person holding control started receiving it: the launcher holds the browser back while they fall behind.

event.name: stop_download

description.summary: the display reads no more of the download

event.description: It was refused, cancelled, or abandoned; the launcher discards the rest of it.

event.name: upload

description.summary: a file from the person

event.description: A file the person is giving the page, whose bytes arrive on the pipe until it closes; the launcher answers stored (all of its size arrived) or failed.

event.name: remove_upload

description.summary: nothing can reach the upload any more

event.description: The display forgot the upload without ever giving its path to the browser (in chosen, or in a drop): the launcher removes it, once it is written if it still is being written.

event.name: chosen

description.summary: a file the person chose for the chooser

event.description: The path the launcher stored an upload at, chosen for this chooser.

event.name: chooser_done

description.summary: the person's choice is complete

event.description: Every chosen file was sent; the portal answers with them.

description.summary: no files: the person cancelled, or nobody holds control

event.name: inspect

description.summary: read the page's structure

event.description: At the admin's request, for the agent: the launcher writes the page's answer to `query` on `answer` as JSON and closes it; closed with nothing written, there is none.

event.name: open_page

description.summary: open a page in place of every page the browser shows

event.description: For the current lease holder, at the admin's request (a public demo's page): the launcher opens `url` (https) in a new tab and, once the browser made it, closes every other tab. Answered with page_opened.

event.name: settle

description.summary: say once the browser has handled the keys sent so far

event.description: After an agent's keys, once the browser has read them (it answered the shell's ping): the launcher answers with settled once the browser's pages have run what they had to run before, the keys among it, so the agent's next keys go where those keys left the focus. With `strict`, after keys the browser itself may act on (a shortcut, a named key), each page that shows also draws a frame first, which it does only behind the keys on their way to it. A browser that takes too long is not waited for.
